title: Grateful Dead Live at Utica Memorial Auditorium on 1973-03-21

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of an early‑73 marathon with a smoking Dark Star, Sunshine, Jack Straw and Wharf Rat, recorded well despite minor mix quirks.
ai_review.review: The performance is energetic and tight, featuring standout moments like a blazing Dark Star, bright “Here Comes Sunshine” and soaring keyboards on “Jack Straw”, while the soundboard source delivers generally good clarity though some vocal levels are low and there’s occasional distortion on “Eyes of the World”. Overall the show is regarded as one of the stronger early‑1973 dates despite a few mix imperfections.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate 4–5 stars and praise the energy, standout songs and overall performance; recording issues are noted but not severe enough to outweigh the strong show quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear SBD with less sterile mix than typical 1973 boards. Vocals are occasionally recessed (especially Jerry’s and the lead on “Eyes of the World”), Bob’s guitar can be overly forward, and water‑damage caused some distortion on the “Eyes” vocals. Overall listenable and better than average for the era.

poor_songs: Dark Star (noted as scattered by a later reviewer)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds with strong openers like “Bertha” and “Box of Rain”, moves through bright mid‑set tunes, then a high‑energy second set with seamless transitions into “Wharf Rat” and a monster Dark Star.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar work praised but mixed low in the recording; occasional lyric clarity issues noted.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass and vocal performance highlighted as strong on “Box of Rain”; also remembered for his quip about no longer playing St. Stephen.
band_member_comments.Bob: Often a bit too loud in the mix; backing vocals mentioned positively.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboard work lauded, especially the mind‑blowing keys on “Jack Straw”.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming described as fluid and integral to the improvisations.
